reasoning_traces.think:
Event Interest \(\mathcal{I}(e,t)\) is defined as a continuous integral of instantaneous interest contributions over time, capturing temporal dynamics of in-game moments. Cumulative Event Interest \(\mathcal{C}(t)\) aggregates these into a scalar timeline signal, enabling temporal segmentation for highlight reels. Game Context Adjustment \(\mathcal{I}_{\text{adj}}(e)\) modifies base interest using conditional probability of outcome changes, distinguishing impactful from trivial events. These primitives form a dual hierarchy: temporal granularity (Event Interest) and strategic significance (Context Adjustment), enabling robust extraction of both highlights and lowlights. Failure modes include overfitting to rare events (e.g., goals) or underweighting skillful but non-scoring plays. The framework avoids monotony via entropy thresholds, ensuring diverse narrative coverage.
